clue.text: Inclination of writer to sing

parts.note: a pen is the instrument a writer uses, standing for the writer
to chant is to sing in a measured, repetitive way

explanation.surface: A tendency in some author to burst into song.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or leaning towards something, the same as an inclination.

clue.text: Smiling kit-bag filler?

parts.note: recalls the wartime song telling soldiers to put their troubles in an old kit-bag and smile

explanation.surface: A cheerful soldier stuffing a duffel bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Pack Up Your Troubles in Your Old Kit-Bag' ends 'smile, smile, smile': the one doing the stowing is grinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stows things in a bag or box is one who fills it, in the song with troubles.

clue.text: Limited quarrel at noon

parts.note: a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A brief argument at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' wants to be ROW; it is the archer's bolt, ARROW, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restricted in scope or width is narrow.

clue.text: Shortly he will ring a greeting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shortly signals the contracted form of will, as in he'll

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Soon he will phone to say hi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a phone call; it is O. 'Shortly' cuts WILL to 'LL, as in he'll.
explanation.definitionFit: A word said on meeting someone, such as hi, is a salutation.

clue.text: African palm-civet found in west, north and in east

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
taken as written
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A tree-dwelling African mammal ranges through west, north and east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in west' belongs to the definition: the animal lives in West Africa, not the letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: The nandine or African palm civet is a small arboreal carnivore of the forests of West and Central Africa.

clue.text: "The Mosaic Path " (Book Two)

explanation.surface: A title and subtitle for a volume about the way Moses led.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mosaic' means 'of Moses', not tiled: the first sense is the Israelites' way out of Egypt under Moses; the second is the second book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The departure from Egypt led by Moses is the road out he followed, and the Bible's second book is named after that departure.

clue.text: Oxy-phenol compound used by wood-tappers

definitions.note: the clue words describe what something is for, an instrument struck on wooden bars

indicators.note: compound, a chemist's word for a mixture, signals the letters combined anew

explanation.surface: A chemical substance that woodpeckers or carpenters rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry of 'Oxy-phenol compound' is a blind; 'compound' rearranges the letters of OXY-PHENOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussion instrument has wooden bars played by tapping with small hammers.

clue.text: Such obstinacy sounds — er.. corrected

indicators.note: corrected implies the letters were wrongly ordered and are now put right

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stubborn speaker hesitates, um-ing and er-ing, before putting it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' looks like a homophone signal but is fodder: 'corrected' rearranges SOUNDS and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dourness is stern, sullen stubbornness, a form of obstinacy.

clue.text: Blue picture?

parts.note: reads as a smutty film, but means a painting of the heavens

explanation.surface: An adult film.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'blue picture' is a pornographic film; here the blue is the sky's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view of the sky is a picture dominated by blue.

clue.text: State of vehicle needing an oil-change

parts.note: a car is a common road vehicle

indicators.note: an oil-change here means the letters of 'an oil' are changed around

explanation.surface: A car in poor condition that is due for an oil change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil-change' looks like garage work; 'change' rearranges AN OIL to OLINA after CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: North and South Carolina are both states of the USA.

clue.text: Knowing our inside, like baker at work

indicators.note: inside says the word our sits within the synonym for knowing

parts.note: fly is informal British for knowing or sharp-witted
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shrewd look at our insides compared with a baker on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY in British slang means knowing or astute; OUR goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker kneading dough gets covered in flour, so is dusted white with it.

clue.text: This sort of party, going to nation, will get us nowhere

definitions.text: This sort of party, going to nation, will get us nowhere

parts.words: This sort of party, going to nation, will get us nowhere
parts.note: the kind of men-only party, joined to the word nation, makes a word for being stuck and going nowhere

explanation.surface: A political party taking its case to the country will achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The party is a men-only celebration before a wedding, not a political party; put before NATION it forms STAGNATION, which gets us nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A men-only party held for a bridegroom before his wedding is named after the male deer.

clue.text: S. Coe on time, almost, going round — he understands resources

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters spinning into a new order

parts.note: the initial S as printed
the surname as printed
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word time loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Sebastian Coe on the track, nearly on schedule as he laps the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TIME to TIM; 'going round' then shuffles S, COE, ON and TIM. S. Coe is the British middle-distance runner.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in economics studies how scarce resources are produced and shared out.

clue.text: Old wars in Cup breaking out

definitions.note: the clue words name conflicts, and the adjective is what describes Rome's wars with Carthage

indicators.note: breaking out suggests the letters are broken up and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Fighting erupts at a cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' rearranges IN CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient conflicts between Rome and Carthage are known by this adjective meaning Carthaginian.

clue.text: Formerly, a royal speedboat destination

parts.note: recalls the folk song in which a bonny boat speeds 'over the sea to' a Hebridean island, carrying Bonnie Prince Charlie into exile

explanation.surface: Somewhere a royal once raced to by fast boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speedboat' splits as the song's line 'Speed, bonny boat': the Skye Boat Song tells of Bonnie Prince Charlie fleeing to this Scottish island in 1746.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides was where the fugitive prince was carried by boat after Culloden.

clue.text: Which lever induces pre, patellar bursitis in reed-organists?

definitions.text: Which lever induces pre, patellar bursitis in reed-organists?

parts.words: Which lever induces pre, patellar bursitis in reed-organists?
parts.note: the swelling over the kneecap (housemaid's knee) is a ..., and the harmonium lever worked with the knee bears that name

explanation.surface: A doctor asks which control is giving harmonium players inflamed knees.
explanation.walkthrough: Prepatellar bursitis is an inflamed swelling in front of the kneecap; a reed organ has a lever pressed by the knee to raise the volume, named for the knee and the organ's swell.
explanation.definitionFit: On a harmonium or reed organ, a lever pushed sideways by the knee opens the swell to make the sound louder.

clue.text: Polish work-place in Derbyshire

parts.note: gloss is a shine or polish
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A workplace in Derbyshire where things get polished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not the nationality but a shine; 'work-place' splits into OP (opus) and the start of the definition. Glossop is a market town in Derbyshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossop is a town in the High Peak district of Derbyshire.

clue.text: Boys must be prepared to observe it

definitions.text: Boys must be prepared to observe it

parts.words: Boys must be prepared to observe it
parts.note: plays on the Boy Scouts' motto 'Be prepared' and the code of conduct members promise to keep

explanation.surface: Lads have to get ready to watch something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be prepared' is the scouting motto, and 'observe' means obey, not watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule-set every Boy Scout promises to keep is their movement's code of conduct.

clue.text: Enhance boat-crew in Orpington, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the rowing crew goes inside the bird

parts.note: Orpington is a breed of chicken, so an example of a hen
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Raising the profile of a rowing club based in a Kent suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Orpington looks like the London suburb but is a breed of chicken, so a HEN, around EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten something is to make it stronger or more intense, raising it.

clue.text: Mild Labour-leader in bond of union

indicators.note: in says the initial letter goes inside the binding substance

parts.note: cement is what binds things together, a bond of union

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: A gentle Labour leader holding a party together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour-leader' looks like a politician, but only the first letter, L, is wanted, put inside CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather or temper is gentle and merciful, which is to say mild.

clue.text: Baked beans need this lid for protection

definitions.text: Baked beans need this lid for protection

parts.words: Baked beans need this lid for protection
parts.note: beans is slang for heads, baked by the sun, and a lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A tin of baked beans has to keep its cover on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beans' are heads and a 'lid' is a hat: sunburnt heads need a pith helmet, a topi in Anglo-Indian English.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun helmet worn in hot countries to shield the head.

clue.text: Mid-off on field in offensive jumper

indicators.note: on places one piece before the next in the down-and-across reading, here first
mid asks for the central letter of the word off

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a field or meadow

explanation.surface: A cricketer fielding at mid-off on the pitch in an unpleasant sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here it means the middle of OFF, F, placed on LEA (field). A 'jumper' is also a British sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a biting parasite that leaps, so it is an objectionable jumping insect.

clue.text: e.g. third man red file revealed

indicators.note: revealed suggests the letters are laid out anew, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret agent exposed in a communist dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third man' looks like the spy film, but is a cricket fielding position behind the slips; 'revealed' rearranges RED FILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Third man is one of the positions taken by a cricket team's outfielders.

clue.text: Sound evidence of a tissue having been thrown out

definitions.text: Sound evidence of a tissue having been thrown out

parts.words: Sound evidence of a tissue having been thrown out
parts.note: the noise 'atishoo' is heard when air is blown out violently, and a handkerchief is wanted

explanation.surface: Proof that a used hankie has been binned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tissue' is said like 'atishoo', the noise of the expulsion, which is the sound evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: The involuntary explosive blast of air from the nose is accompanied by an 'atishoo' noise.

clue.text: My hits could be mighty in it

definitions.note: the words describe a place by the strong man working there

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be rearranged to form another word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blacksmith boasts that his blows would be powerful in the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's poem: 'Under a spreading chestnut tree the village smithy stands; the smith, a mighty man is he'. 'could be' rearranges MY HITS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Longfellow's poem the blacksmith working in the village forge is a mighty man.

clue.text: Encourages some of our gestures

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the movements we make with our hands are meant to spur others on.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to push or encourage them to act.

clue.text: In 2 way, you spend millions for a fictitious title

indicators.note: in a way (the 2 is the page's misprint of 'a') here means the letters are put into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Spending a fortune to buy yourself a made-up rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spend' looks like the action, but YOU, SPEND and M are rearranged by 'In a way', which the scan prints as 'In 2 way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name or alias is an invented name used in place of one's real one.

clue.text: Livelong day that precedes spring?

indicators.note: that precedes puts the abbreviation in front of the water source

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A whole long day before the season of spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is the water source, not the season; 'Livelong' read as 'live long' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or linger somewhere for a long time.

clue.text: Refuse to have young

explanation.surface: Declining to start a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun (rubbish), not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropped rubbish is waste in the street, and an animal giving birth to several young at once does so in one batch.

clue.text: Fan sticking

explanation.surface: A supporter who stays loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause is a fan, and something that clings to a surface is attached to it.

clue.text: Yarn-bearer led off after victory

indicators.note: after says the rearranged piece follows the synonym for victory

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: off here means the word led is disordered

explanation.surface: Someone telling tales leaves after a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a tall story, but is thread wound on a reel; 'off' rearranges LED to DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A windle is a reel or spindle on which spun thread is wound.

clue.text: Comic show — extremely daffy — gets big wave inside

indicators.note: inside says the long breaker goes within those outer letters
extremely asks for the first and last letters of daffy

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave

explanation.surface: A zany comedy turn in which a huge wave crashes on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives the first and last letters of 'daffy', D and Y, around ROLLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is comic entertainment or a humorous performance.
